quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Moving away from them may make them return to your lane too soon. The center is the safest position.

questions.question: You should not move to the far side of your lane when being passed because it:

options.text: Stops the passing driver from returning to your lane too early.
Makes the passing driver return to your lane too early.
Makes the passing driver complete the pass faster.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the passing driver return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane encourages the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Push the handgrip on the side you want to turn. Push the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars when it rains. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk freely whenever they want.

questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet to keep you focused on riding. They should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you avoid?

options.text: Base travel segment lengths on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so everyone reaches their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so everyone reaches their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Base trip length on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Lean your shoulders with the turn.
Sit as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before turning, slow down by closing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: You may need less following distance if:

options.text: The road surface is slippery.
You cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions. This includes slippery pavement, heavy traffic, or when you cannot see ahead. You need less distance only when conditions are perfect.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of total stopping power.

questions.question: What is the right footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces.
Shoes with short heels.
Shoes with tall heels.
Always sneakers.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: When a group of riders enters a highway, they should:

options.text: Enter one at a time in a line.
Enter in a staggered formation.
Enter in pairs.
Stop and wait for all traffic to clear so everyone can enter together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Enter one at a time in a line.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation, but should switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following you too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following you too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down if someone is following too close. They may not see the hazard ahead that is making you slow. Also flash your brake light when slowing in places where drivers don't expect it.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right part of your lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane before passing to see better and be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Keep your headlight on.
Reduce your following distance.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at intersections and ride in a lane position that makes you easy to see. Keep space around you so you can move quickly if needed. Never assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.
